A_target.statement:
Let $f: C_\bullet \to D_\bullet$ be a [[Definition:Chain Map|chain map]].
Then $f$ induces a well-defined [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphism]]:
:$f_*: \map {H_n} C \to \map {H_n} D, \quad \eqclass z {} \mapsto \eqclass {\map f z} {}$

B_source.statement:
Let $B \subseteq Z$ and $B' \subseteq Z'$ be [[Definition:Submodule|submodules]].
Let $f: Z \to Z'$ be a [[Definition:Module Homomorphism|homomorphism]] with $\map f B \subseteq B'$.
Then $f$ induces a homomorphism $Z / B \to Z' / B'$.

substitutions.the ambient subobject: the cycles, the kernel of the boundary map
substitutions.the collapsed sub-subobject: the boundaries, the image of the next boundary map
substitutions.a map preserving both: a chain map commuting with the differentials

derived.independence of representative: cycles differing by a boundary have images differing by a boundary

validity_conditions: The identity d . d = 0 places the boundaries inside the cycles, so the quotient defining homology exists.
A chain map commutes with the differentials, hence carries cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries.
Preserving both subobjects is exactly the hypothesis needed for descent, so the induced map is well defined and independent of the chosen representative.
proof_plan: As $\partial \circ \partial = 0$, the [[Definition:Boundary (Homology)|boundaries]] $B_n = \Img {\partial_{n + 1} }$ are contained in the [[Definition:Cycle (Homology)|cycles]] $Z_n = \map \ker {\partial_n}$.

As $f$ is a [[Definition:Chain Map|chain map]], $\partial f = f \partial$.
If $\partial z = 0$ then $\partial \map f z = \map f {\partial z} = 0$, so $f$ sends cycles to cycles.
If $z = \partial w$ then $\map f z = \partial \map f w$, so $f$ sends boundaries to boundaries.

By the source result, $f$ descends to a homomorphism:
:$Z_n \paren C / B_n \paren C \to Z_n \paren D / B_n \paren D$

Hence $f_*: \map {H_n} C \to \map {H_n} D$ is well defined on [[Definition:Homology Group|homology classes]].
{{qed}}
